bb.name: Regional Manager
bb.description: Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Start a regional manager: a long-lived thread that takes on a body of work and hands each piece to a crew thread. Open its panel in the navigation rail and press New: bb's own new-thread composer opens, already set to a fresh worktree and auto permissions, and the goal you type starts the thread. It plans, keeps its memory in a folder of markdown files on the bb server, and starts crews: child threads that each work on their own branch, on its provider and model, from its brief and done-criteria, with the crew rules and the memory index in their first message. Told to propose crews and wait, it describes them in a question on its board instead, and starts them once you answer. It messages, reads and closes its crews, and sets itself reminders, once or repeating (in two hours, at a time, every day), that wake it with its own note when they come due; it can list and cancel them. When only you can decide something, it puts a one-line question with up to five options on its board and keeps working: you choose an option or answer in your own words there, never in a form in its thread, and the panel's rail entry counts it with every crew under Needs you on the boards the panel lists. A crew ends its work with one handoff (done, blocked or gave up, with what it did, its evidence, concerns, deviations and findings), stored whole. Every done handoff is checked by an independent verifier the plugin starts itself: a hidden thread in the crew's environment, on another model when bb has one, that runs what proves each done-criterion and returns a verdict with the output as evidence. The plugin itself checks that the claimed commit is checked out on a clean tree, reading the crew's environment through bb's git plugin as it hands off, never through the verifier's shell: anything else fails the verdict, and a read bb can't make leaves it unverified, with no fix round spent. When the crew has a pull request, a verdict that passed every criterion waits under Verifying until CI finishes on the claimed commit, and fails if CI fails. A crew's first failed verdict goes straight back to it: the plugin sends each failed criterion and its evidence to the crew's thread as a message from the verifier, and the crew fixes it and hands off again for a new check. A second failure goes to the regional manager, which messages the crew, asks you, or replaces it with a fresh crew that starts from its brief and its latest findings. The plugin then wakes the regional manager with a short message that names what happened and never quotes a crew; a done handoff reaches it only with its verdict, and its catch-up returns every update in full. It is also woken when a crew fails, waits on you or stops without a handoff, when a crew's pull request opens, merges or closes, its CI passes or fails, or a review approves it or asks for changes (read through gh every minute while CI runs, else every five), when you save a memory file, switch verification or answer one of its questions, and when one of its reminders comes due. A switch on the New page and on the board turns verification off for one regional manager, for handoffs made after it. Its Board, a tab in the thread and a page in the panel, shows that switch, why PR status is unavailable when gh can't read GitHub, its digest, its open decisions under Needs you and answered ones under Done, and every crew under Needs you, Ready for review, Verifying, Working, Landing, Idle or Done, live, each linked to its thread and to its pull request with its CI; a verified handoff waits under Ready for review with ✓, or under Landing while its pull request is open, a merged one is Done, one that failed again after its fix round or couldn't be verified under Needs you with ✗ or the reason, each with its verdict a click away (every criterion, its result and evidence, and the verifier's model), an unchecked one as Unverified, and a blocked one under Needs you. bb can't stop the regional manager from editing files itself, so the plugin detects it: when one of its turns ends with changed files in its own environment's working tree, read through bb's git plugin, its board shows a warning and the thread is woken to hand the change to a crew, once per number of changed files; a turn that ends with the tree clean clears the warning. It is detection, not a guarantee: a change it committed isn't seen, and nothing is blocked or reverted. Each row in the panel also opens a Memory editor over the same files; every write names the version it replaces, so neither you nor the thread can silently overwrite the other. Unsaved Memory edits and unsent answers to its questions stay in the browser, through a resize or a reload, until you save or send them.
